Level 3 · Advanced · Week 1

Save Points: Git Basics

Git is a save-game system for code: every commit is a save point you can go back to.

What you will learn

  • Use Terminal to move between folders.
  • Make save points (commits) with git and give them helpful messages.
  • Look back in time with git log, spot changes with git diff, and undo mistakes with git restore.
  • Warm up your Level 2 skills: functions, lists and loops.

The big idea

In a video game, a save point lets you try something risky. If it goes wrong, you load the save and try again. Git gives your code save points. Each save point is called a commit. Every commit has a short id (like a1b2c3d) and a message that says what changed. Together the commits make a timeline: the story of your project.

Saving takes two moves, like taking a class photo:

Terminal survival kit

Terminal is a chat window with the computer: type a command, press Return, read the answer.

Type this It means
pwd Where am I? (print working directory)
ls List the files in this folder.
cd git-quest Go into the folder git-quest.
cd .. Go up one folder.
Tab Finish a long name for you. Type cd git-q and press Tab.
⟦k⟧↑\uparrow⟦/k⟧ Bring back the last command, so you do not retype it.

The six git commands

Command What it does Game words
git init start a save system in this folder new save file
git status what changed since the last save? pause menu
git add hero_badge.py choose what goes in the next save pack your backpack
git commit -m "Add star" make a save point with a message save the game
git log –oneline list the save points, newest first load-game menu
git diff show exactly what changed spot the difference
git restore hero_badge.py throw away unsaved changes reload last save

TipStuck in a strange screen?

If you typed git commit without -m, git opens an editor called Vim. Press Esc, type :q! and press Return. Then try again with -m "your message".

Good commit messages

A good message finishes the sentence “This commit will …”. Start with a verb, keep it short (50 letters or fewer) and say what changed.

 Not helpful  Helpful
stuff Add jump to hero
update Make star twice as big
fixed it Fix score going below zero

Exercise1.2: Commit Coach

Folder: week01/ex-commit-coach. Finish the functions in starter.py:

  • is_good_message(message) returns False for empty, too long, boring or one-word messages.

  • make_message("add", "star shape") returns "Add star shape".

  • find_secrets(lines) returns the lines that contain words like password or api_key.

Check with check_my_work.py. Then Run it and test 3 messages of your own.

Exercise1.3: Log Reader (if you finish early)

Folder: week01/ex-log-reader. Teach Python to read the text that git log --oneline prints. Each line is a commit id, a space, then the message:

line = "5b7a913 Fix hero walking through walls"
parts = line.split(" ", 1)   # split only at the FIRST space
print(parts)   # ['5b7a913', 'Fix hero walking through walls']

Finish parse_log, count_commits, find_commits and oldest_first. Extra: paste your own git log --oneline into SAMPLE_LOG.

TipSafety: history remembers everything

Git writes your user.name and user.email into every commit, forever. Use a nickname and an @example.com email. Never commit passwords, real names, addresses or photos of people. Deleting a file later does not delete it from the history.

New words

git
A program that keeps save points of a folder, so you can look back and undo.
repository (repo)
A folder that git is tracking. Git keeps its notes in a hidden .git folder inside it.
commit
A save point: a snapshot of your files plus a message and an id.
commit message
A short label that says what changed, like “Add jump to hero”.
commit id
The short code name of a commit, like a1b2c3d .
diff
The differences between two versions: - lines were removed, + lines were added.
Terminal
An app where you type commands for the computer.

Homework: Save Points

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CoreInventory Review + one commit (about 10 minutes)

  1. Open week01/hw-inventory-review/starter.py in Thonny. A game backpack is a list like ["gem", "key", "gem"].

  2. Finish the three TODOs: count_item, remove_all (make a new list) and most_common.

  3. Git practice: copy your finished starter.py into Documents/git-quest, then in Terminal:

    cd ~/Documents/git-quest
git add starter.py
git commit -m "Add inventory review"
git log --oneline

How many commits does your git-quest have now? (blank to fill in)

ChallengeMessage makeover

Rewrite each unhelpful message so that a friend would understand it. Start with a verb.

Unhelpful Your better message
stuff (made the hero jump higher)
asdf (added a sound when you score)
fix (score no longer goes below 0)

Then use your Commit Coach from class to test your three messages. Do they all say “Great message!”?

CreativeA badge with a history

Change hero_badge.py in your git-quest folder at least 3 times: new colors from the palette, a bigger star, a second ring, your own hero name (made up, never your real name). Commit after every change. Then draw your timeline below: one circle per commit with its message.
